answers.children: Yes — Irish Setters are good with children because their playful energy matches a child’s and their gentle nature leads them to use careful nudges rather than rough play. The breed’s affectionate temperament makes them lean into family members for attention, while their large 60-70 lb frame and stamina from bird hunting days suit energetic outdoor games with kids. Their high energy can sometimes overwhelm smaller children during indoor romps. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Irish Setters usually get along with other pets thanks to their sociable and affectionate disposition, though their high energy can annoy more reserved dogs. Bred as bird-hunting pointers they show limited prey drive towards household companions, and their gentle heart helps them coexist peacefully when given daily exercise to burn off enthusiasm.
answers.exercise: Irish Setters need one to two hours of vigorous daily exercise such as long runs or field-style fetch sessions that replicate their bird-hunting stamina. Without this their boundless energy turns to destructive chewing of items like boots. Their elegant frame and exceptional stamina make them suited to hikes where they cover extra ground darting back and forth.
answers.shedding: Yes — Irish Setters shed moderately with heavier seasonal sheds. Their long silky coat with feathering tangles easily and spreads fine red hairs around the house, requiring regular grooming to stop mats forming behind the ears and on the tail. The coat’s texture traps loose hair from their energetic movements.
answers.hypoallergenic: Irish Setters carry a long, silky red coat with heavy feathering on the legs, chest and tail that sheds year-round and leaves hair on everything it brushes past. No breed is genuinely hypoallergenic, and the Setter is not among those suggested to allergy sufferers — the feathering holds dander until grooming releases it.
answers.training: Irish Setters are moderately easy to train because their intelligence and playful temperament respond to trick-based work that channels their bird-hunting instincts. Their high energy and occasional scatterbrained enthusiasm can make them hard to focus during sessions, so owners must provide mental stimulation such as hidden toys or new commands.
answers.lifespan: Irish Setters live 12-15 years. Their health robustness is affected by the demands of their high-energy build developed for hours of field work, and the profile notes they can be prone to specific health issues that owners must monitor to support a full lifespan.
answers.size: Irish Setters reach 60-70 lb and stand 25-27 in tall. Their elegant frame with flowing silky coat feels substantial when a 65 lb dog leans affectionately for pets or tries to climb into a lap despite its large sporting build originally developed for locating game birds.
answers.barking: Irish Setters do not bark a lot. Bred to silently set or crouch when pointing birds they tend to stay quiet indoors, using their energetic enthusiasm for play rather than vocal alerts, though occasional barking occurs if they become bored from lack of exercise.
answers.apartment: No — Irish Setters do not suit apartment living. Their high energy from bird-hunting days leads to restlessness and destruction if not given one to two hours of vigorous daily runs, and their affectionate playful nature means they struggle to settle quietly indoors without ample mental and physical outlets.
answers.first-time: No — Irish Setters are not a good first dog. Their high energy that can be overwhelming and the daily commitment to vigorous exercise plus grooming of the long silky coat create demands that challenge novices, despite the breed’s affectionate and gentle heart with families.
